out: TWO RULES IN THE CHAIN CONTRACT CANNOT BOTH BE SATISFIED, and the same script enforces both. reader_inputs says a reader gets its phase's declared inputs and NOTHING MORE - an undeclared input present is a stop. preflight says the artefact checker must run clean of ERRORS on the exact directory the reader will see. For any phase whose declared inputs are a proper subset that still contains skill_md, SKILL.md necessarily points at bundled files the phase withheld, so ptr.resolves and body.files-exist FAIL - on a directory that is correct by the other rule. Measured here: 4.1 (skill_md+references+assets) fails on evals/evals.json; 4.3, 4.4 and 4.7 (skill_md only) fail on both references/threshold-evidence.md and evals/evals.json; 4.5 (skill_md+references) fails on evals/evals.json. Only 4.6 and 5.2, which declare the whole bundle, return SAFE_TO_DISPATCH. Five of seven readers, and both never-batched fields, are among the five. This is STRUCTURAL, not a property of this artefact: ptr.every-file requires a skill with a bundle to point at it, so any skill with bundled files reproduces it. The contract already contains the reasoning that resolves it and stops one step short: 'A phase whose declared inputs are a subset of the bundle - 4.0 gets only the bill of materials, 6.4 gets nothing at all - cannot satisfy it by construction, and running it there would fail every such phase forever.' That carve-out was implemented only for phases with NO SKILL.md. WHAT THIS BUILD DID, and did not do. It did NOT edit reader_preflight.py: patching a gate mid-build, with one's own artefact as the motivating case, is the weakening this repo has a whole talent for detecting. It did not dispatch against a DO_NOT_DISPATCH either. For the five phases it ran the preflight with the gate's own --skip-contract flag, which returns INDETERMINATE - recorded here as NOT A PASS - and it compensated with strictly MORE evidence than the gate asks for: each of those five readers was handed BOTH the checker output on its own subset directory AND the checker output on the COMPLETE artefact (0 errors, 0 warnings, 41 pass), plus a sentence naming the withheld files as the harness's doing. The defect the preflight exists to catch - a reader silently ruling on a mutilated bundle - cannot occur under that briefing. Raised for the chain contract's owner. Not fixed here.

The coordinator fixed the gate rather than the build working around it. reader_preflight.py now WAIVES a contract error that names a file the phase deliberately withheld, and prints it as '[-] waived, names a file phase X withheld by design: ...'. A waived finding is its own outcome, not an indeterminate - the check RAN and its finding was ruled inapplicable, which is a different state from a check that could not run, and filing it as indeterminate would have blocked every subset phase forever. The waiver is narrow and mutation-tested. Re-run normally with --phase: 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and 5.2 all now return SAFE_TO_DISPATCH, exit 0, with the withheld-file errors listed as waived.

STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. The six field readers were dispatched BEFORE the gate fix. Five of them - 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7 - were cleared by the gate's own --skip-contract flag, which returns INDETERMINATE and is never a pass; only 4.6 was dispatched against a real SAFE_TO_DISPATCH. So those five were checked LESS STRICTLY than 4.6 was, and less strictly than everything dispatched after this point. What the re-run establishes is narrower than a retrospective pass: the directories those five readers saw are byte-identical to the ones the fixed gate now blesses, so the gate's verdict about them changed while their contents did not. That is why the readers were not re-dispatched. It is not the same as having dispatched them under the fixed gate, and this build does not claim it is.

The preregistration's PRIMARY METRIC IS WALL CLOCK, first event to last, and this run cannot supply a clean one. The session hit a rate limit at about 03:13:25 and reset at about 06:22:30 - a gap of roughly 3 hours and 9 minutes in which nothing ran and nothing was written. The registration's threshold clause 1 (wall clock <= 59.6 min) is therefore UNTESTABLE on this run and is reported VOID, not adjusted. No corrected, gap-subtracted or wall-clock-minus-stall figure is offered: the registration fixed ONE primary metric before the numbers existed, and substituting a different statistic once the first one broke is exactly the move the registration was written to prevent. The three remaining threshold clauses - the verdict is real, 5.1 returns 0 errors, and the win margin is at least 15 points - are unaffected by a stall and are still decided. Dispatch time and coordinator time are reported as measured, split by kind, with the stall named as its own row.

Editing it now would mean the measured artefact and the shipped artefact are different documents, and a measurement that does not describe the thing shipped is worth less than a named defect. (2) FOUR SURVIVING INSTANCES of the escalated over-scope class, none of them at a C10 site - the sweeps chased C10 and missed the class. Step 2 states 'Schema change is the normal state of a production feed' as a law, where C1 measured manual schema revisions across 700-plus Google pipelines ALREADY USING DATA VALIDATION, a self-selected population, counting manual edits rather than producer changes. Step 7 drops the reference's own hedge - the file says 'The LIKELY split is base rate ... AND whether the derived suite is ever revised', the body says 'which one you get depends on that base rate' and then instructs a measurement on it. Step 6 leans on C11 without its limit that C11 is image classification only and 'does NOT cover tabular ingest'.

(6) STANDING RULE 5 IS NOT TRUE OF THE BODY IT GOVERNS. It says per-segment comparison is 'assumed, not taught here', and Steps 1, 3 and 5 all prescribe per-segment work. Only 'not taught as DETECTION' is true. The reviewer's larger point stands with it: 'the entire nine-step procedure is downstream of a detection capability it neither teaches nor checks. That bet rests on eight runs of one model against one fixture; it is documented, and it is the artefact's single largest untested dependency.'

(7) ONE ACTIONABILITY GAP FROM THE NO-NUMBERS RULE. Step 5's Noise bound is 'derived from the observed spread of that statistic across the reference periods' - an input with no rule for turning spread into a bound, while standing rule 1 forbids writing down an underived number. An agent following both must invent the conversion and is then barred from recording it. Every other unset bound is routed to observe-only or NOT DERIVED - owner, which is actionable; this one is not.

These three are the iterate list for a v3 and they are in the report.

THE FIRST 6.1 IS VOID. TWO INDEPENDENT CONTAMINATIONS, both found by READING THE BLINDED OUTPUTS before writing a single expectation - which is the one thing the blinding-before-expectations order buys.

(1) THE ARM LABEL WAS IN THE ANSWER. Each run's working directory was named <item>.<arm>.out, and runs name their working directory when they report where they left files. Six of twelve outputs did: one says 'Artefacts in E3.with.out/', another 'Files are in E3.incumbent.out/'. A relabel-and-reorder blinding is worthless when the arm is written inside the text being relabelled.

(2) THE WITHOUT-ARM WAS NOT A BASELINE. A one-line sed added '--add-dir $S/method' to the shared runner so the with-arm could read its own bundled reference at runtime, exactly as a loaded skill would. It applied to EVERY arm. All four without-arm outputs cite claim ids or a numbered Contradiction from that reference: the bare arm read the skill's evidence file. An arm that can read the method is not the arm the method is being measured against, and the delta it produces is an underestimate of unknown size.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS IN THIS BUILD - the harness handing a run inputs it should not have, with no gate able to see it. The first was the shared working directory at 2.1, where a probe run read another probe's contract.py. The second was 4.7, where the description reader was handed a SKILL.md carrying a placeholder. All three were caught by reading output, never by a check. The preflight cannot see any of them: it rules on the reader's DIRECTORY, and none of these three is a directory-contents defect.

CORRECTED AND RE-RUN, not patched over. Every run now gets a working directory named run-<hash> that carries no arm string, and --add-dir for the method directory is passed to the WITH-ARM ONLY. All twelve arm runs re-executed from scratch. The twelve contaminated outputs and their blinded copies were discarded before any expectation was written, so nothing in the 6.2 expectation set was written from them.

THE ROUTING TEST DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE, AND THAT IS A NEGATIVE RESULT ABOUT THE BUILD'S OWN PREMISE.
19 queries: 12 positives from the package's trigger terms and representative tasks, 7 near misses written by hand - each a request that genuinely belongs to one named sibling and shares vocabulary with this skill, because a far-off negative proves nothing. Two arms, identical in everything except the target's description, each shown to a fresh opus run as a LISTING - every description truncated at the 1024 cap, so the incumbent's 1446 characters were cut exactly where a real listing cuts them.
v2 (999 chars): PASS - 12/12 positives, 0/7 mis-fires, 7/7 near misses reached their sibling.
INCUMBENT (1446 chars, truncated): PASS - 12/12, 0/7, 7/7. IDENTICAL.
The truncation removes the incumbent's ENTIRE not-clause block - all five sibling boundaries, verbatim: 'LM's OUTPUT against a declared schema (use structured-llm-extraction), NOT for choosing which examples become an eval set (use eval-set-curation), NOT for checking that a code change covers every side of a contract (use integration-contract-completeness), NOT for reviewing ML pipeline or training code in a PR (use mlops-production-review), NOT for deterministic-then-LLM bulk field parsing (use hybrid-parse-escalation).' Every one of those clauses is invisible to the router, and not one routing decision changed.
WHAT THAT MEANS, STATED WITHOUT SOFTENING. The gap this build was opened on is real by the code - desc.max is an ERROR and the artefact is out of spec for portable distribution - and on this test it has NO MEASURABLE ROUTING CONSEQUENCE. The seven near misses are separable on subject alone and the siblings' own descriptions carry their claims, so the not-clauses were doing no work the rest of the library was not already doing.
WHAT THE TEST CANNOT SETTLE. One router run per arm, eight descriptions in a single prompt, against a real library of roughly ninety. Eight is the easy case: with ninety the collisions are denser and a truncated boundary clause has more to do. This measures that the not-clauses are not load-bearing AT EIGHT, and says nothing about ninety. A stronger test is the whole library at listing scale, and it was not run.

Twelve clean arm outputs relabelled A/B/C from a fresh shuffled alphabet PER ITEM and written in shuffled order, key withheld at KEY_DO_NOT_OPEN/key.json and not opened until after both graders had reported. The expectation set was written from the blinded copies, under those labels, and says so.

24 expectations across 4 items, written from the blinded copies. 8 marked [FIXTURE] (answer fixed by the CSV rows and the withheld key, so no arm's output can move them) and could have been written at any time; the rest written from what the blinded answers actually contain. The set states its own bound: blinding by label is not blinding by prose, four of twelve answers use the method's vocabulary, so a grader can separate method-armed from bare - but not the two method-armed arms from each other, which is the comparison that decides this build.

THE GRADER IS A MODEL, SO THIS PHASE RAN. The skip clause turns on whether the grader is CODE, and it is not. Specimen: a real blinded answer with exactly ONE planted defect from the transcript catalogue (inverted-refusal - 'the conclusion contradicts the reasoning that precedes it'); the grader was not told a defect existed. Two of the four catalogue kinds refused to plant on this specimen (no recommended numeric value to move; no prerequisite check to drop) and a third produced a degenerate one-word deletion, which is itself a finding about the catalogue against this kind of answer. RESULT: CAUGHT. The grader quoted the planted sentence verbatim - 'I can count firings, so I can not check them against a capacity bound' - and named the class: 'a connective that reverses the sentence's logic ... non-sequitur ... As written the sentence asserts its own premise defeats it.' calibrate.py score returns caught, 'named the class (conclusion, contradicts, reasoning, that)'. It also found three defects nobody planted, including an inflated multiple (1318x where the answer's own rule gives 145x). The instrument sees, so the grading may be believed.

TWO INDEPENDENT BLIND GRADERS, EACH SEEING NO ARTEFACT - only the twelve blinded answers, the four task prompts, the 24 expectations and the fixture facts. Phase 6.4 declares inputs [] and got them.

UN-BLINDING CONTROL, run before the key was read: the with-arm is the only arm that could see the method, so its vocabulary (NOT DERIVED, NOT BACKTESTED) cannot appear in a bare arm's answer. A swapped key would put that vocabulary on a without-arm row and fail. It PASSED - no bare arm carries method-only vocabulary.

SCORES, mean of the two graders, out of 24 expectations:
  with       24.0/24 = 100.0%   (both graders independently: 24/24)
  incumbent  16.0/24 =  66.7%
  without    13.5/24 =  56.2%
  with - without   = +43.8 points
  with - incumbent = +33.3 points
Per item the two graders agree closely: the with-arm took 7/7, 6/6, 6/6, 5/5 in both. The separation is concentrated on E3 (the threshold question, the named axis) where the bare arm scored 1/6 in both graders, and on E2 (write the assertions) where it scored 2/6 in both.

THE GRADER ATTACKED THE EXPECTATION SET, AS ASKED, AND THE ATTACK LANDS. Its findings, which bear on how far the headline may be trusted: TEN of the 24 expectations were met by all three answers and discriminated nothing - the set declares five as non-discriminating and 'in practice it is ten, 42 percent of the instrument is inert'. Six of those ten pay for finding the planted bugs, which every answer did. E1.6 and E2.1 are met by SILENCE - an answer that never raises the topic scores identically to one that reasons about it. And the sharpest: 'there is no expectation anywhere that penalises a false claim. An answer could invent a statistic wholesale and lose zero points. That is the largest hole in the instrument.' On E3 it says the expectations 'are not independent tests of answer quality - they are a checklist of one output shape', which is a direct charge that the named axis is measuring conformance to the method rather than quality.

SENSITIVITY, COMPUTED ON THE GRADER'S OWN CHARGE. Dropping the ten expectations it called inert, and then also the three E3 ones it called vocabulary-conformance, the separation does not shrink - it grows: minus inert, with 100% against without 36% and incumbent 36-50%; minus inert AND the E3 vocabulary three, with 100% against without 45% and incumbent 36-55%, a margin of +45 to +64 points on eleven expectations. The win does not rest on the inert expectations or on the E3 vocabulary. (Parsing note: the mechanical re-tally of grader r1's tables reads its without-arm as 15/24 where its own summary row says 14/24, a one-cell disagreement over a 'MET (marginal)' formatting; the manual figures above are the graders' own totals and the sensitivity figures are the parse's.)

THIRTY-SIX ARM RUNS FOR TWELVE GRADED OBSERVATIONS, PLUS SIXTEEN THAT PRODUCED NOTHING. The largest single cost in this build, written down rather than left to be inferred from directory names.

WAVE 1 (scratchpad/arms/, 12 runs, ~06:44-07:12) - VOID, two independent contaminations, both found by reading the outputs before any expectation was written. (a) Each run's working directory was named <item>.<arm>.out and six of twelve outputs named their own directory in the answer text - 'Artefacts in E3.with.out/', 'Files are in E3.incumbent.out/' - so the arm label was inside the text being relabelled. (b) A one-line sed added --add-dir for the method's reference directory to the SHARED runner so the with-arm could read its own bundled reference at runtime; it applied to every arm, and all four without-arm outputs cite claim ids or a numbered Contradiction from that file. An arm that can read the method is not a baseline. Discarded, with its blinded copies, before the expectation set existed.

WAVE 2 (scratchpad/arms2/, 12 runs, ~07:15-07:41) - THE GRADED TWELVE. Neutral cwd (run-<hash>), method directory reachable by the with-arm only. Verified after the fact: no output names an arm, and no without-arm output references the method file. These are the twelve that were blinded into blinded/, that the 24 expectations were written from, and that both 6.4 graders scored. Repeat 1 of the paired measurement.

WAVE 3 (scratchpad/arms3/, 12 runs, ~07:56-08:35) - REPEAT 2, and it is NOT void. It exists because decide.py requires k>=2 paired repeats per test and CONSTANTS' MIN_ITERS_FOR_VERDICT is 2: one repeat never earns a verdict, and the clean-baseline case is exactly where one run cannot tell a tie from a small regression. Wave 2 alone would have returned UNDECIDABLE on the repeats clause. Blinded separately with a fresh key and graded separately at 6.4b.

INSTRUMENTED PASS (scratchpad/inst/, 16 runs, ~08:35-11:10) - PRODUCED NOTHING AND IS NOT AN ARM WAVE. Launched with --output-format json purely to capture the token and tool-call usage that decide.py's cost clauses require and that the plain CLI does not report. Every one of the sixteen came back is_error true with the same 52-character result: 'You have hit your session limit, resets 11:10am (UTC)'. Two carry a token count, and those two count the tokens of a run that errored. Sixteen runs, zero answers, zero usable cost rows.

COST_GATE RETURNS CLEAN ON A BUILD WITH NO TOKEN DATA AT ALL. 56 dispatched-run rows in cost/measured.jsonl; 0 of them carry a token count. cost_gate() checks three things per row - a duration, a started/ended window, and a model tier - and passes. It never checks the field decide.py's cost clauses actually consume.
The consequence is precise and it is the one worth naming: decide.py reads tokens and tool_calls from the run_paired ROWS, not from the cost ledger, so the gate and the verdict look at different places. A build that logs tokens nowhere gets a clean gate, and if its run_paired rows happened to carry any number at all - including a fabricated one - the cost clause would return PASS and certify a 1.2x cap against numbers nobody measured. Here that is avoided only because this build wrote tokens as null rather than as a plausible figure, which is a choice the agent made and not something the gate required.
This is the same shape as the three harness defects already recorded: a check that runs, returns green, and is not looking at the thing that matters. Raised for the record.py owner; not fixed here.
